blocks.text: Platform Process Guide
Applicant provider and admin walkthrough with account labelled screenshots

Follow the process from the applicant action to the responsible provider or admin action and then back to the applicant. Each walkthrough identifies the account, the record to open, prerequisites, controls, expected result and next owner. Use specialist roles first; manager and superadmin views remain last.

Use Talunaw Campus Pathways Grant to start a new application while intake is open. Use the separate closed-intake rounds for screening, formal verification, examinations and interviews. For current DSS use Talunaw Scholar Selection Round or Talunaw Assessment Completion Round. For recurring support use Talunaw Learning Continuity Grant; for a one-time award use Talunaw Study Essentials Award.

Current hosted additions were verified on November 13, 2026, Manila time. Earlier screenshots are retained where the workflow is unchanged. Dates printed on an existing record are fixed; they do not move automatically each day. Do not change the clock or move selection activities into an open intake to bypass a prerequisite.

Current DSS, support and admin handoff screenshots below were captured from hosting with the account named beside them. Older screenshots marked as isolated examples illustrate guarded branches that the tester has not yet created on hosting. Opening a form did not submit its decision. No existing account, award, payment or tester decision was reset for this update.

All listed accounts use password123 for this private demonstration. Applicant photos are the platform silhouette. Use fictional supporting files and payout details. A saved payment or distribution record is not evidence of a real transfer; external payments, refunds and email delivery are not performed by this guide.

Provider and admin account groups

Talunaw and Sidlakbay both have these specialist logins: .programs, .reviewer, .selection, .decisions, .recipients, .monitoring, .releases, .profile, .team, .support, and .billing. Add the organization prefix talunaw or sidlakbay, for example talunaw.selection. The .newstaff accounts show first-login setup. Both organizations also have a .manager account and a representative login using the organization prefix alone.

The admin specialist logins are demoops.accounts, demoops.reviews, demoops.support, demoops.billing, demoops.finance, and demoops.records. The organization awaiting verification is hirayalon. Manager and governance accounts are listed in the last four processes.
1 Registration and sign in
Signed in account: Not signed in
Page shown: Registration form before sign in

A new applicant or provider starts at registration, selects the appropriate account type and supplies the requested identity and contact information. Follow the email verification instructions before continuing. An existing demo account instead signs in using its username or email. The middle initial is optional.

Applicant: registers and completes profile evidence. Provider: registers the organization and submits its verification information. Admin: operational accounts are managed through the authorized admin account workflow; provider and applicant verification are handled by demoops.reviews. No new account was registered for this screenshot.
2 Applicant profile and supporting evidence
Signed in account: demo.student.profile
Page shown: Applicant profile and supporting evidence

The applicant maintains identity, contact, education, household, and location details. Section edit modals keep the applicant on their record. Upload documents that support the profile rather than merely filling the text fields.

Applicant: complete the record and evidence. Provider: later sees the submitted applicant record and which information is self-declared. Admin: the review officer verifies the profile evidence before the applicant can apply.
Edit the applicant information in its modal
Signed in account: demo.student.profile
1. Choose Edit beside the personal information section.
2. Update only the details that need correction and check the required fields.
3. Review the changes before Save changes; Cancel leaves the record unchanged.
4. Photo changes can save immediately through the photo controls, so do not replace or remove a photo merely to demonstrate the form.
3 Admin applicant verification
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
Page shown: Admin applicant verification

The review officer checks supporting files first. In the academic record review, Academic results contains the grading scale and verified result; accepting that document saves any correction. Step 2 then records only the overall profile outcome and review note. Accepting evidence does not verify the whole profile or select an applicant for a scholarship. Use demo.student.verification for this queue and demoops.reviews to review it.

Applicant: demo.student.verification supplies or corrects evidence. Provider: cannot replace platform profile verification with a scholarship decision. Admin: demoops.reviews performs verification; superadmin is not the normal operational reviewer.
Open the applicant verification record
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
1. Select Brenel Dumayun from Applicant verification. Confirm the name and account before reviewing.
2. Read the review guide for the current step. Expand the complete profile only when more context is needed, and check any changes since the previous decision.
3. Go to Supporting evidence and compare each required document with the corresponding declared information.
4. Uploaded files do not verify the whole profile. Review current evidence first; use the queue navigation to keep the original search and filters while opening the next record.
Review an individual supporting document
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
1. Select Review beside a submitted document to open this evidence-review dialog.
2. Inspect the file and related self-declared profile details. OCR is only a suggestion; use the larger preview if needed.

3. For an academic record, choose Accept document and confirm or correct the grading scale and verified result in Academic results. For an unreadable or unsuitable file, request a replacement and explain why.
4. Acknowledge the comparison, then accept the document to save the academic result and evidence decision together. This leaves overall profile verification pending.
Record overall profile verification
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
1. Return to the applicant record after reviewing the individual files and photo.
2. At Step 2 Final profile decision, confirm that all current required evidence is accepted. Grades were already reviewed in Academic results; there are no grading controls here.
3. Choose Verify profile, Request profile correction, or Keep under review for the profile as a whole. Add the final review note; correction and reopening require an explanation.

4. Save decision records only the overall profile outcome, not grades or a scholarship result. An outdated form is rejected if the record changed. Reload, compare the changes and review the current evidence before submitting again.
4 Provider organization profile
Signed in account: talunaw.profile
Page shown: Provider organization profile

The organization profile manager maintains the provider information shown to applicants, including identity, public description, branding, contact information, and location. A provider preview shows the applicant-facing presentation.

Applicant: discovers and evaluates providers. Provider: talunaw.profile maintains the organization record and evidence. Admin: demoops.reviews checks registration evidence and organization verification.
5 Admin provider verification
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
Page shown: Admin provider verification

Use demoops.reviews to review the Hirayalon organization. Step 1 reviews each current proof separately: open Review, inspect the file beside the organization details, then Accept document with the comparison acknowledgement or Request replacement with a clear reason. Step 2 records the final provider account decision only after every current file is accepted. Verification does not approve the provider's scholarships.

Applicant: sees the provider trust state. Provider: sees individual file outcomes and corrective notes, and uses Replace document to submit new proof. Admin: records each document review and then a separate account outcome; the final account decision never overwrites file outcomes or notes.
Review organization documents individually
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
1. Sign in as demoops.reviews. Open Provider verification and select Hirayalon. Step 1 shows each file as Awaiting review, Accepted, or Needs replacement, with reviewer and date when available.

2. Choose Review on one file. Compare the submitted proof with the legal organization name, registration authority and number, and representative details. Download it if the format cannot be previewed.

3. Choose Accept document only after inspecting it and checking the comparison acknowledgement. Otherwise choose Request replacement and explain what must be corrected. Saving records the reviewer, time, note and file revision; it does not verify the account.

4. Repeat for every current file. Unreviewed files, unavailable files and replacement requests block final approval. If another reviewer or upload changes the file, reload instead of submitting an outdated review. The screenshot shows an unsaved form.
Record the final provider account decision
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
1. In Step 2 Final provider account decision, confirm all current proof has been individually accepted. Uploading documents alone is insufficient.
2. Choose Approve, Reject, or Return to pending. Rejection requires a clear organization review note. File outcomes and their notes remain independent.
3. Save decision only when appropriate. If the organization or document set changed, reload and inspect the current record before deciding.

4. Organization verification is not scholarship publication or applicant selection. Existing approved demo accounts are not reset by this update; inherited historical file approvals do not count as individual reviews during a new verification.
Replace organization proof after a review
Signed in account: hirayalon
1. Open Organization profile then Legal verification. Review the status and corrective note for the affected file.
2. Choose the Replace document icon on that row. The upload form identifies the file being replaced and selects its document type. Choose the new file and acknowledge the upload terms.
3. Upload proof replaces the old file with a new unreviewed record. The new file does not inherit acceptance. Other unchanged accepted files keep their own decisions.

4. New proof or relevant legal identity changes return approved accounts to review. Relevant organization changes invalidate prior file comparisons; a reviewer must inspect the current details and files again.
6 Program creation and publication
Signed in account: talunaw.programs
Page shown: Program creation and publication

The program coordinator prepares scholarship details, benefits, eligibility rules, requirements, selection stages, dates, applicant limits, and branding. Drafts and requested changes stay separate from published programs. The staged editor validates each step.

Applicant: sees published scholarships, not private drafts. Provider: talunaw.programs prepares and submits programs. Admin: demoops.reviews checks publication submissions; it does not make the provider final applicant selection.
Configure documents and the formal application handoff
Signed in account: talunaw.programs
1. Open a program, choose Edit, and open Application in the staged editor.
2. Configure the pre-screening files, optional files and post-qualification requirements appropriate to the program.
3. Set formal handoff instructions, deadline and the official link or physical venue with its map pin where needed.
4. Choose common document requirements from the selector and type only provider-specific requirements. Review the remaining steps before saving or submitting.
7 Admin program review
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
Page shown: Admin program review

The program review queue separates publication checks from organization verification and applicant verification. The officer examines the program information and requests changes or records the publication review decision.
Applicant: can discover approved published programs. Provider: answers requested changes. Admin: verifies the submission through the program review workspace.
Inspect the submitted scholarship before publication
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
1. Open a program from Program review and confirm its provider and submission status.
2. Review the advertised support, eligibility, requirements, dates, selection process and recipient terms.
3. Read the readiness checks and changes since the previous review, then approve a valid submission or request clear changes with a review note.
4. Save only after checking the current submission. If another user changed it, reload before deciding. Publication is separate from selecting a scholarship applicant.
Define qualifications and the scoring plan
Signed in account: talunaw.programs
Program configuration determines admission safeguards and later assessment. Use a draft when demonstrating a change; do not change an intake that already has fixed evaluation snapshots.

1. In Eligibility, choose the intended education level and qualification, grade scale, year level, location and other rules. Remove irrelevant inherited restrictions rather than relying on free-text descriptions.
2. Separate mandatory rules, reviewable qualifications and preferences according to the available controls. A preference contributes guidance; it is not the same as a mandatory exclusion.
3. In the selection setup, choose the actual screening, formal verification, exam, interview and final decision stages needed by the program. Explain their order to applicants.
4. Inspect the preset weights for the scored stages. Submission freezes the scoring plan for that intake; formal application is a qualifying check, not extra numeric points.
5. Review support terms, deadline order, recipient slots and application intake limit before submitting the draft. Publication review remains an admin decision.
Expected result and handoff: The published program supplies clear rules and a stable evaluation basis. The admin reviewer checks publication readiness separately from applicant selection.
8 Scholarship discovery and preparation
Signed in account: demo.student.apply
Page shown: Scholarship discovery and preparation

Use Search and filter to find published scholarships, then open View details to review benefits, eligibility, required files, deadlines and application instructions. Each result displays the scholarship logo beside its name; background photographs and provider logos are separate assets. Apply starts the application only when the verified profile meets the required rules and applications are open. Use the provider link to inspect the organization.

Applicant: demo.student.apply is ready to start a new application. Provider: supplies accurate program and organization content. Admin: oversees publication and trust checks, not the applicant choice of scholarship.
Submit a new scholarship application
Signed in account: demo.student.apply
Use the open Talunaw Campus Pathways Grant. The account already has a verified profile; completing an application is a new tester action.
1. Open Scholarships, select View details, then read How to apply, Eligibility, Requirements and the deadline. A suggested match percentage is preparation guidance, not approval.
2. Choose Apply. Review the current profile and eligibility checks. Use the eligibility link for details; do not proceed by entering a false value to satisfy a rule.

3. For a reviewable exception, follow the available explanation and evidence controls and wait for the relevant review when required. A hard unmet rule or an unverified profile cannot simply be ignored.
4. Choose current files from My Documents or upload the required files. Complete program questions and any declarations or terms required by the form.
5. Review the complete application and confirm submission. Open Applications afterward and inspect the saved requirements, current stage and next-action guidance.
Expected result and handoff: A submitted application appears in the provider review queue. It is not yet screened, selected, accepted for support or paid.
9 Reusable applicant documents
Signed in account: demo.student.apply
Page shown: Reusable applicant documents

My Documents holds reusable files for future applications. A saved document is not automatically an accepted application requirement; the applicant must choose appropriate current files during an application.

Applicant: uploads and manages documents. Provider: reviews files actually submitted to its program. Admin: profile evidence verification remains separate from a provider application document decision.
10 Submitted application and next action
Signed in account: demo.student.screening
Page shown: Submitted application and next action

The application details tell the applicant the current stage, what happens next, required submissions, schedule, decision, and history. demo.student.screening is waiting for the initial provider review.

Applicant: follows the next-action guidance and answers correction requests. Provider: talunaw.reviewer checks eligibility and submitted documents. Admin: handles platform verification or oversight, not routine scholarship screening.
11 Provider screening and document review
Signed in account: talunaw.reviewer
Page shown: Provider screening and document review

The application reviewer works from the assigned queue instead of the manager overview. Review the applicant record, eligibility and document evidence before recording a screening result. Corrections should identify what the applicant must fix.

Applicant: demo.student.screening is the prepared screening record. Provider: talunaw.reviewer performs the review. Admin: demoops.reviews verifies profile evidence separately; passing screening does not itself award a scholarship.
Inspect application eligibility after selecting an applicant
Signed in account: talunaw.reviewer
1. Open Darel Kalimbas from My review queue and confirm that the application is assigned to you.
2. Compare the declared profile against each program rule. Review unresolved items rather than relying only on an overall score.
3. Inspect the Profile tab and supporting evidence where a claim needs checking.
4. Hard requirements and reviewable qualifications must follow their configured policy; resolve the relevant review before recording a screening result.
Review the application evidence
Signed in account: talunaw.reviewer
1. Open Evidence in the selected application record.
2. Use View or the file preview to inspect the submitted file, then select Review beside that document.
3. Record an evidence status and specific review notes appropriate to the file. An upload alone is not accepted evidence.
4. Repeat for the required files before relying on document readiness for the screening result.
Record the screening result or request correction
Signed in account: talunaw.reviewer
1. Open Result in the selected application record and check the readiness messages.
2. If information is missing, open Request correction and identify what the applicant must change.

3. Review the rubric, record its required scores and explanation, and choose the screening outcome. On a scored intake, the academic-merit and financial-need criteria supply the frozen screening component; eligibility checks and document acceptance still have their own safeguards.
4. Save the appropriate review or result only after completing its prerequisites. Claiming an unassigned application is a separate access action.
Return a correction to the provider reviewer
Signed in account: demo.student.screening then talunaw.reviewer
Use this branch only after the reviewer requests a specific correction. The request and each saved response remain part of the review history.
1. As the applicant, open the application next action or Requirements section and read the correction note and response deadline.
2. Replace only the requested files or correct the permitted information. Profile changes that invalidate platform evidence may need renewed profile verification.
3. Review the corrected submission, acknowledge its terms where required and confirm Send update. A replacement does not inherit the prior file acceptance.
4. As talunaw.reviewer, open the returned record from the review queue, inspect the changes and current evidence, then record the review or result.
Expected result and handoff: The corrected application returns to review. A correction response does not pass the stage automatically.
12 Formal application verification
Signed in account: demo.student.formal
Page shown: Formal application verification

Formal application is a configured stage for providers that require a further official application or in-person verification. Applicants follow the published instructions and schedule where applicable. A separate session is not always mandatory for this stage.

Applicant: demo.student.formal follows the formal instructions. Provider: talunaw.selection records the verification, required proof and result according to the configured stage. Admin: can inspect selection activity evidence through oversight.
Record the formal application verification
Signed in account: talunaw.selection
1. Select Elani Talagsik from the formal-application work queue.
2. Read the published handoff instructions and verify the actual formal application requirements or originals.
3. Complete the required stage verification and attach provider proof where requested. Use a session only when the configured formal workflow needs one.
4. Record the stage outcome after the prerequisites are satisfied; a published instruction is not proof that verification happened.
13 Examination and interview scheduling
Signed in account: talunaw.selection
Page shown: Examination and interview scheduling

The selection officer assigns eligible applicants to sessions. Separate sessions support different dates or venues; online interviews use a meeting link. Session attendance or completion and an individual applicant result are different records.

Applicant: demo.student.exam.assign or demo.student.interview.assign awaits assignment. Provider: talunaw.selection manages sessions and outcomes. Admin: demoops.reviews can inspect selection activity records and evidence.
Create assign and complete a selection session
Signed in account: talunaw.selection

Use Firan Magsilay for exam assignment, Jovin Rimayag for interview assignment, or Harel Salinaw for a conducted exam awaiting completion. They are different prepared starting points, not one person already at every step.
1. Open the relevant closed-intake program and selection workspace. Create a session using its form or modal. Choose the stage, date, start and end times, capacity and instructions.
2. For an onsite activity, enter the venue and selectable map pin. For an online interview, choose Online and provide the meeting link. Use separate sessions for different venues, dates or groups.
3. Assign only applicants who have reached the correct stage. Publish the session and check the roster. Applicants read or acknowledge their own assignments; capacity and program scope still apply.
4. After the activity actually occurs, record attendance for each assigned applicant and upload the required provider proof for that session or person.
5. Use the session completion control once its checks are satisfied. Then open each applicant result separately and record the actual assessment score and outcome.
Expected result and handoff: A completed schedule with attendance and proof enables result recording where required. It does not automatically pass everyone or issue a scholarship offer.
14 Applicant examination schedule
Signed in account: demo.student.exam.confirm
Page shown: Applicant examination schedule

The applicant reads the assigned examination date, venue, instructions, and acknowledgement action. Other prepared accounts cover completing the conducted session and recording an individual examination result.

Applicant: demo.student.exam.confirm acknowledges the schedule. Provider: demo.student.exam.complete is the session-completion scenario and demo.student.exam.result awaits a result, both acted on by talunaw.selection. Admin: provides oversight rather than taking the examination decision.
Record the conducted examination result
Signed in account: talunaw.selection
1. Open Ivara Dalimpon in the results queue and inspect the assigned examination and readiness checks.
2. Check attendance or participation and the required completion evidence for the conducted session.

3. In a scored intake, enter the actual examination score and maximum score with the passing outcome, then review the confirmation. Older unscored applications can retain their original result without invented assessment points.
4. Session completion and an individual applicant result are separate actions; do not pass an applicant simply because the schedule exists.
15 Applicant interview schedule
Signed in account: demo.student.interview.confirm
Page shown: Applicant interview schedule
The interview schedule tells the applicant when and how to attend, including the meeting link for an online interview. An applicant acknowledgement does not prove the interview took place.

Applicant: demo.student.interview.confirm acknowledges its schedule. Provider: talunaw.selection records attendance, stage proof and the interview result; demo.student.interview.result is ready for that result. Admin: can inspect supporting activity records.
Record the interview result
Signed in account: talunaw.selection
1. Open Luvan Silambay from the interview results queue.
2. Check that the interview actually occurred and review participation, stage proof and any recorded interview notes.
3. Record the interview assessment score and maximum when the frozen scoring policy requires them, together with the stage outcome. Do not substitute an attendance status for a numeric evaluation.
4. An online meeting link or applicant acknowledgement is a schedule instruction, not evidence that the interview was completed.
16 Recording conducted stage results
Signed in account: talunaw.selection
Page shown: Recording conducted stage results

The results workspace separates work ready for result recording from scheduling work. Complete the required conducted-session or stage verification and attach proof where required before recording an applicant result.

Applicant: sees the recorded result and next stage. Provider: records the evidence-based result and any permitted audited correction, rather than merely marking every applicant complete. Admin: oversight does not replace the provider stage result.
17 Final scholarship decision
Signed in account: talunaw.decisions
Page shown: Final scholarship decision

The decision officer compares fully evaluated applicants within the same scholarship against its remaining slots. The DSS combines the frozen screening, exam and interview evaluations and suggests selection or waitlisting. It never makes the award decision. Earlier exam or interview success alone is not a scholarship award.

Use demo.process.dss.first, demo.process.dss.second and demo.process.dss.third in Talunaw Scholar Selection Round for current DSS. All three are awaiting the tester decision. Talunaw Assessment Completion Round contains demo.process.dss.score with an interview score still to enter. The older demo.student.decision application remains a legacy manual example.
Open the final decision form
Signed in account: talunaw.decisions
1. As talunaw.decisions, open Pending decisions, choose Talunaw Scholar Selection Round, and select Nerali Salindaw. Read the evaluated score, rank, review guidance, capacity and prior stage results.
2. Confirm that the comparison is Ready to compare. There are three complete evaluations and two unfilled slots. Review the stage breakdown; a profile matching percentage is not this selection score.

3. In Record final outcome, choose the actual decision and add the required notes or internal rationale. A different suggestion or a cutoff tie can require an explanation. A waitlist suggestion is not an official waitlist entry until saved.

4. Review the confirmation and save only the intended outcome. If another decision or score changed, reload the comparison. Selection reserves capacity and sends the offer; it does not accept the agreement for the applicant or release money.
Compare final candidates using the DSS
Signed in account: talunaw.decisions
Choose Talunaw Scholar Selection Round. Nerali Salindaw, Veylan Marahuyo and Amirel Talahir have completed scored prerequisites and no final outcome. Two slots remain.
1. Open Pending decisions and select this program. Ready to compare means the intake is closed and all current candidate evaluations needed for the comparison are complete.
2. Inspect scores 94.8, 90.6 and 85.0, their ranks and the two remaining slots. The first two suggestions are Consider selecting; the third is Consider waitlisting.
3. Open the small evaluation-breakdown icon. Compare frozen screening, examination and interview components and their weights. These are recorded evaluations, not the applicant matching percentage.
4. Open Record decision for the intended candidate. Follow the result controls and confirmation. Enter a clear internal reason if departing from guidance or resolving a cutoff tie.
5. Return to Pending decisions after saving. Capacity and suggestions update. Equal scores can share a rank; an unresolved tie at the cutoff must not be arbitrarily treated as an automatic winner.
Expected result and handoff: The officer owns the official outcome. Selecting creates an offer, waitlisting creates the official queue, and an unsaved suggestion changes neither.
Read the scored stage breakdown
Signed in account: talunaw.decisions
The example uses screening 30 percent, examination 40 percent and interview 30 percent. Other configured stage combinations use their own frozen preset.
1. Open the evaluation-breakdown icon for Nerali Salindaw.
2. Read the stage status, score, maximum and weight. Screening reuses the reviewed academic-merit and financial-need rubric components.
3. Treat formal verification as a prerequisite. It is not counted twice as additional points.
4. If a stage is incomplete or its result was reopened, review it through the responsible workspace before relying on the final total.
Complete a missing evaluation before ranking
Signed in account: talunaw.selection then talunaw.decisions
Use Sorevi Lindawen, demo.process.dss.score, in Talunaw Assessment Completion Round. The interview happened and passed, but its numeric evaluation is deliberately missing.
1. As talunaw.selection, open the completed interview through selection history, then the assigned applicant record. Confirm participation and the original assessment evidence.

2. Expand Earlier stage evaluations in the applicant record. Beside Interview, choose Add score and enter the actual score and maximum. Add a factual note and review the confirmation before recording it.
3. To correct an existing evaluation later, use the correction control and give the required explanation. Earlier score revisions stay in history.
4. As talunaw.decisions, select this program in Pending decisions. A final score appears only after all scored and qualifying prerequisites are complete. Missing does not mean zero.
Expected result and handoff: The comparison uses the latest valid recorded evaluation. Completing a score still leaves the final scholarship outcome to the decision officer.
18 Applicant acceptance of the agreement
Signed in account: demo.student.agreement
Page shown: Applicant acceptance of the agreement

The selected applicant reviews the actual recipient terms before accepting or declining. Acceptance creates a clear record of the obligations the applicant agreed to; later program edits must not silently replace those accepted terms.

Applicant: demo.student.agreement is awaiting its agreement response. Provider: talunaw.recipients tracks agreement responses. Admin: independent review later uses the accepted source, not an unrelated current program rule.
Read and respond to the recipient agreement
Signed in account: demo.student.agreement
1. Open the selected application and choose Review agreement.

Select a recipient and open the monitoring checklist

Set up and activate the monitoring plan
Signed in account: talunaw.programs or talunaw.manager
The plan is the reusable support policy. A published check-in is the actual recipient appointment. Talunaw Learning Continuity Grant already has an active plan to inspect without replacing it.
1. Open the program monitoring plan. In Schedule, set the review frequency, support start and end dates, grace period and whether extension or exception requests are allowed.

Publish a check in for the selected recipients
Signed in account: talunaw.monitoring
Use New check-in from the active Learning Continuity Grant plan. Inspect the form without publishing if you only want to demonstrate its controls.

2. Name the period, academic year and appointment. Set the actual date, time, venue, original documents to bring and short recipient instructions.
3. Choose the intended accepted recipients from the roster. Keep separate sessions or recipient arrangements for different dates and venues instead of publishing overlapping appointments.
4. Review the recipient count and instructions, then confirm Publish check-in only when ready. Cancel leaves the current data unchanged.
5. Sign in as an assigned applicant and open Scholarship Support then Check-ins. Confirm that the appointment and required originals appear for that applicant.
Expected result and handoff: The chosen recipients receive their appointment. A plan alone, an unassigned roster entry or a published date is not attendance or completed review.
Record attendance originals and case closure
Signed in account: talunaw.monitoring
The attended-group roster has a record awaiting verification, one awaiting closure and one already completed. Select the person before opening an item.

1. For a new actual appointment, record Attended only after the applicant attends. If the appointment changes, use the reschedule controls and notify the recipient instead of pretending the old meeting occurred.
2. For Nivara Kalumay, open Current academic record and inspect the physical original. Record the verified grade, scale, result and notes. Repeat for enrollment.

3. If an extension, exception or follow-up is genuinely needed, record it through the available request or follow-up controls and resolve it before normal closure. Do not mark a pending item met to remove the blocker.
4. Select Elvian Silaraw. Both items are already met. Choose Close check-in, review the outcome and confirm it. The applicant can then read the closed result.
Expected result and handoff: Check-in closure records a period outcome. The Recipient Officer still makes any renewal, completion or other support decision separately.
22 Admin monitoring oversight
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
Page shown: Admin monitoring oversight
The review officer can inspect monitoring records and supporting evidence through its own oversight workspace. This is separate from routine provider checklist review.
Applicant: brings the required records. Provider: records attendance, document results, and any follow-up. Admin: inspects the saved record without replacing the provider result.
Inspect the exact support record as an admin
Signed in account: demoops.reviews
Admin monitoring oversight is an inspection and oversight workflow, not a shortcut for a provider document result.
1. Open Monitoring oversight and select the Learning Continuity Grant recipient or period rather than stopping at totals.
2. Inspect appointment, attendance, individual requirement results, provider notes and review history.
3. Use the available admin review controls only for their stated oversight purpose. A separate case review requires its own notice, evidence and response process.
4. Return the operational next action to talunaw.monitoring or talunaw.recipients. Do not claim an admin observation confirms receipt of a benefit.
23 Renewal completion and support decisions
Signed in account: talunaw.recipients
Page shown: Renewal completion and support decisions

Open Calira Maranaw (demo.process.support.decision) in Talunaw Learning Continuity Grant as talunaw.recipients, then Support status. The check-in is closed and both cash allowance and mentoring receipts are confirmed. Renew support to continue the award, or Complete support after the agreed work is finished. For an early end, record the effective date, notice date, and reason. A decision based on an agreement concern still requires the applicable independent review and appeal opportunity. Do not use this form to record voluntary withdrawal; review the recipient request in Section 27.

In practice, the award terms determine whether support ends at graduation, at the end of a term, or through an early decision. A period ending without renewal is not the same as ending it early. Some programs require final documents before the last release. See UP Diliman DOST-ASTHRDP procedures and CHED Merit Scholarship guidelines on notice and appeal.

Review outcome opens the decision and available response options. Benefit totals are saved with new closeouts and also appear in Support history. Later receipts update the benefit record, not the saved totals. Older decisions without saved totals still link to benefit records.

1. For Calira, open Support status. Check the completed review, accepted agreement and benefit settlement. Choose Renewed only when the provider intends to continue support.
2. Record a matching reason category, effective date, renewed support end, next review and the next-period terms. Review the confirmation before saving.

3. Sign in as the recipient. Open Support history and the renewal outcome, then read its dates, reasons and terms. Use the acknowledgment or permitted response rather than accepting a different current program page.
4. To demonstrate a response without first recording another provider outcome, use Revian Talihim and the existing renewal history shown below.

25 Recording actual benefit distribution

Signed in account: talunaw.releases

28 Agreement concerns before conclusions
